trace.title: External route
trace.detail:
## Understand the idea

Pods can be replaced and their addresses can change. A Service gives a stable access abstraction for matching endpoints.

Selectors connect the Service to labelled Pods; a spelling mismatch can leave no endpoints.

Ingress or Gateway-related resources describe external routing under a selected controller implementation. Defining an Ingress object does not install every required controller or cloud load balancer.

The exact controller’s contract matters.

Map DNS, ports, targetPort, ready endpoints, network policy, and app listener separately. Inside a Pod, localhost refers to its network namespace.

Reaching a peer service uses the service name, not the browser’s public URL by habit.

trace.title: Follow one item
trace.detail:
Client/edge → controller route → Service port → selected ready Pod endpoint → app target port. A 503 can come from no eligible endpoints even when a pod process exists.

Test a selector mismatch, wrong targetPort, and readiness failure separately. Observe how each changes events/endpoints/response.

Keep the app’s allowed-host/proxy/TLS configuration in the path.

trace.title: Try the failure
trace.detail: A container listening only on 127.0.0.1 may not accept the intended Pod-network traffic. An Ingress without its controller is only desired routing data.
